claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has an FCC structure.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is nanocrystalline and has high hardness.
The coating has stable wear resistance at 300 K.
Atomic-size differences in HEAs produce severe local lattice distortion that impedes dislocation motion.
Severe lattice distortion is responsible for stable room-temperature wear in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Increasing temperature lowers the free-energy barrier for kink-pair nucleation on screw dislocations through an increasing thermal-entropy contribution.
A critical temperature is reached when thermal energy overcomes the kink-pair nucleation barrier for screw dislocations.
The stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrCoCu decreases as temperature increases.
Low stacking-fault energy at room temperature stabilizes partial-dislocation separation in the coating.
Elevated temperature causes screw-dislocation glide to dominate deformation in FeNiCrCoCu.
At elevated temperature, dislocation slip can replace twinning as the dominant deformation mode.
Thermal activation significantly reduces the critical friction stress for screw-dislocation motion.
A critical friction stress of approximately 1.3 GPa occurs at 300 K in a similar alloy system.
Freely moving screw dislocations bypass strengthening from lattice distortion and stacking-fault structures.
Uncontrolled screw-dislocation glide causes rapid lattice softening and lattice disorder.
Wear resistance and elastic modulus decline sharply above the critical temperature.
The high-temperature transition changes sliding from a stable low-friction regime to unstable high-wear behavior.
The relevant softening threshold may occur above 600 K or within the interval from 300 K to 1000 K.
Twinning dominates at cryogenic temperatures rather than at elevated temperatures.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says a thermally induced reduction in SFE enables dominant screw glide, while the mechanism also says low SFE stabilizes separated partial dislocations. It does not explain why a further SFE reduction would reverse that stabilizing effect and favor screw glide.

The conditions suggest a threshold above roughly 600 K, but the uncertainty field acknowledges that no FeNiCrCoCu threshold is measured and that the cited temperature trend only comes from a different alloy simulated at 300 K and 2000 K.
